patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient was brought to the emergency department because of sudden, painless loss of vision in her right eye that occurred 30 minutes ago while watching TV. She has a history of coronary artery disease, hypertension, and type 2 diabetes mellitus but has had trouble adhering to her medication regimen.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with sudden loss of vision in one eye.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“I had sudden, painless loss of vision in my right eye about half an hour ago while I was watching TV.” “I didn’t have any pain or other symptoms.”

Thank you for that information. To help narrow this down, did you notice any warning signs right before the vision loss, such as flashes of light, a sudden shower of floaters, or a dark curtain-like shadow moving across your field of vision?

“Earlier, I didn’t notice flashes of light, a sudden shower of floaters, or any curtain-like dark shadow— it just suddenly went out in my right eye.” “I haven’t had any pain or other symptoms since it happened.”
Could you please tell me your age and whether you have any history of high blood pressure, diabetes, high cholesterol, or atrial fibrillation?
“I’m 60 years old. I have high blood pressure and type 2 diabetes, and I also have coronary artery disease; I’m not sure about atrial fibrillation, but I do have trouble sticking to my medications.”
Is the vision loss in your right eye completely blacked out, or is it partially blurred or missing in a specific area (such as the top or bottom half)?
“It’s mostly completely gone in my right eye—like it just went black all at once. The left eye is seeing normally.”
Have you experienced any recent headaches, scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing, or unexplained fever or weight loss?
“No, I haven’t had any headaches, scalp tenderness, jaw pain when chewing, fever, or any unexpected weight loss.” “It’s just the sudden black-out vision in my right eye, and nothing else.”
Have you experienced any brief, temporary episodes of vision dimming or loss in that same eye over the past few days or weeks?
“Over the past few days or weeks, I don’t think I had any brief episodes or temporary dimming in that right eye—it just happened suddenly and has stayed gone since then.”
[DDX] Central retinal artery occlusion, Nonarteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy, Vitreous hemorrhage, Retinal detachment, Giant cell arteritis
